correctness.rationale: Companion Fibonacci matrix A∈GL2(Z) induces an invertible integral (r+1)×(r+1) action on homogeneous polynomials of degree r. Its monic characteristic polynomial has constant coefficient ±1, so each r-th-power Fibonacci window obeys an integer reversible recurrence, proving all-shift gcd equals gcd of W0,…,Wr and that gcd divides D0=F_k^r via Dn=F_{n+k}^r−F_n^r. For odd r,k, an odd p dividing gcd implies F_k≡0, F_{k+1}^r≡1, while Cassini gives F_{k+1}²≡−1 mod p, contradiction. Fibonacci parity period3 and modulo4 period6 force gcd2 exactly when k≡3 (mod6), otherwise1. Independent exact gcd loop checked 105 odd-(r,k) pairs r=1..13,k=1..29 with 15 extra windows and finite-prefix equality; no finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Guyer–Mbirika prove the first-power sequence; Mbirika–Spilker prove square powers and explicitly discuss higher-power questions. Neither covers the all odd-exponent/odd-window dichotomy. Unimodular recurrence and Cassini sign parity provide a new uniform proof beyond observed shared low-power outputs.
residual_risks: An independent all-odd-power theorem in older number-theory literature could be expressed in Pisano-period or recurrence-sequence terms and may have escaped the searches.
The classification is restricted to odd r and odd k; for even r, e.g. r=4 k=25, a factor 5 can divide every sum, so no extension is claimed.
The finite prefix reduction is valid for all positive r,k, but the 1/2 dichotomy is not.
